steps.prompt: A calculator says $47 \times 38 = 1786$. Add the digits of each number. Is there a link?

cards.title: Digit sums keep score
cards.body: From Unit 9, a number has the same remainder by $9$ as its digit sum. That remainder is the number’s "nine-score". Nine-scores add for sums and multiply for products, so you can check an answer by checking its nine-score.

try.prompt: What is the remainder when $22$ is divided by $9$?

steps.text: Both are $4$, so the answer passes. (Swapped digits still pass, so it is a quick check, not a proof.)

cards.title: When it fails
cards.body: If the nine-scores don’t match, the answer is certainly wrong. $47 \times 38 = 1796$? $1796 \to 23 \to 5$, not $4$: wrong.

prompts: Casting out nines can say "wrong" for sure, but only "probably right". Why?
